text: PR #5440 merged as 8c5a6a546. While investigating a Windows CI failure in the docs-only #5439 (a stale pre-existing flake in test_polyglot_python_sidecar, confirmed by clean rerun, unrelated to that PR's content), found and fixed a real test-hygiene gap in #5427's own regression test: it cleaned up its moved-aside temp file but not the replacement file its hook writes back at the original path, leaving a stray file in the shared root directory. Confirmed via inspect_and_open_physically_contained_path()'s Windows CreateFileW(FILE_SHARE_DELETE) that the rename genuinely succeeds on Windows, not just POSIX, so this wasn't theoretical. A Copilot review caught a follow-on gap in my first fix (cleanup_error was ignored, so a failed removal would silently defeat the fix) -- fixed to assert cleanup succeeds. Session summary: this closes out a long chain starting from the user's mid-session request to reconcile the migration-pipeline v1-blocking reclassification (#137/#138/#139/#140/#141/#1076/#1077, PR #5437) and finish the #5409 atomic check-and-read migration series (#5426/PR #5428, #5427/PR #5436), plus this cleanup tail (#5439, #5440). Open, non-blocking follow-ups: #5434 (shared read-and-revalidate-path helper), #5435 (launcher-inventory error-code granularity), #5438 (Windows containment-widening error-code reclassification), #5429/#5430/#5431/#5432/#5433 (external_process_policy.cpp/CopperfinStudioHostBridge.cs/build-installers.yml security findings from Codex's earlier broad review, none yet started). None of these are currently selected as next work.
